title: Convert between whole-number percents, fractions and decimals (50% = 1/2 = 0.5 = 50:100)

lesson.title: Percent, Fraction, Decimal — Three Ways to Say the Same Thing

steps.say: You already know that percent means parts out of one hundred, and you can colour it in on a ten by ten grid. Today we take that same coloured grid and learn to write it three ways: as a percent, as a fraction, and as a decimal.

visual.caption: One hundred little squares — fifty of them coloured in

steps.say: Look at the grid. Fifty of the one hundred squares are coloured. So we can say fifty percent. We can also write it as the fraction fifty over one hundred. And because hundredths go in the second place after the decimal point, fifty hundredths is written zero point five zero, which is just zero point five. All three are the very same amount — exactly half the grid.

visual.caption: Fifty percent, fifty hundredths, one half — same picture

steps.say: Let us try a shopping one. A hoodie at the mall in Kelowna is twenty five percent off. Twenty five percent means twenty five squares out of one hundred are coloured, so the fraction is twenty five over one hundred. Written as a decimal that is zero point two five. And if you divide the top and bottom by twenty five, twenty five over one hundred becomes one quarter. So the store is taking off one quarter of the price.

visual.caption: Twenty five squares out of one hundred — one quarter of the grid

steps.say: Now here is the trap lots of kids fall into. Someone sees five percent and writes zero point five. Let us check it on the grid. Five percent means only five little squares out of one hundred are coloured — hardly any. But zero point five means fifty squares, half the whole grid. Those are not the same at all! Five percent is five hundredths, so the five has to sit in the hundredths place: zero point zero five. The little zero right after the point is doing an important job — it holds the tenths place empty.

visual.caption: Five percent is only five tiny squares — nowhere near half

steps.say: So here is the trick that never lets you down. Put the percent number over one hundred to get the fraction, then read that fraction as hundredths to get the decimal. Always ask yourself: is my answer out of one hundred squares? That check catches the decimal point mistake every time.

visual.caption: Fifty percent and twenty five percent shown together on one hundred squares

lesson.answer: A percent is just a fraction over one hundred — and hundredths means two places after the decimal point, so 50% = 50/100 = 0.5 and 5% = 5/100 = 0.05.

practice.question: A winter jacket at a store in Vancouver is 30 percent off. Draw a ten by ten grid of one hundred squares and colour in thirty of them. Then write thirty percent as a fraction over one hundred, as a fraction in simplest form, and as a decimal.
practice.answer: Thirty squares out of one hundred are coloured. Thirty percent equals thirty over one hundred; dividing top and bottom by ten gives three over ten; and as a decimal it is zero point three. (Careful — it is not zero point zero three, because thirty hundredths is the same as three tenths.)
